subject: english
question: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: **Not in my line**

options.text: Not related to my area of expertise

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Not related to my area of expertise .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Not in my line"** refers to something that is outside of an individual’s professional or personal expertise or area of knowledge.
 
• In the context of the given options:
 
 
• **Option 1:** Beyond my authority – This indicates a limitation of power or control but is unrelated to expertise.
 
• **Option 2:** Not related to my area of expertise – This correctly captures the meaning of the idiom.
 
• **Option 3:** Not aligned with my values – This refers to personal beliefs, not professional expertise.
 
• **Option 4:** Below my status – This implies a judgment of social or professional rank, which is unrelated to the idiom.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is Option 2.

Correct Interpretation: *When someone says "It’s not in my line," they mean that the task or topic is not within their knowledge or skills area.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Idioms Related to Expertise:**
 
 
• **"In my wheelhouse":** Refers to something that is within one’s area of expertise or comfort.
 
• **"Out of my depth":** Indicates a situation where someone lacks the necessary knowledge or skills.
